name: Proving the Formula for Rho in Terms of Squared Deviations
problem:
Let's derive the following result:

$$
\rho = \dfrac{S_{xy}}{\sqrt{S_{xx} \cdot S_{yy}}}
$$

We start with the definition of the correlation coefficient $\rho\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho  & =\frac{\text{Cov}(x,y)}{{\sigma }_{x}\cdot {\sigma }_{y}}\end{aligned}
$$

We have

$$
\textrm{Cov}(x,y) = \dfrac1n \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (x_i-\overline{x})(y_i-\overline{y}) = \dfrac{S_{xy}}{n}.
$$

Similarly,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{x} & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{{S}_{xx}}{n}} \\ {\sigma }_{y} & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y})^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{{S}_{yy}}{n}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into our definition for $\rho,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho  & =\frac{\text{Cov}(x,y)}{{\sigma }_{x}\cdot {\sigma }_{y}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{{S}_{xy}}{n})}{\sqrt{\frac{{S}_{xx}}{n}}\cdot \sqrt{\frac{{S}_{yy}}{n}}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{{S}_{xy}}{n})}{\sqrt{\frac{{S}_{xx}\cdot {S}_{yy}}{{n}^{2}}}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{{S}_{xy}}{n})}{(\frac{\sqrt{{S}_{xx}\cdot {S}_{yy}}}{n})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{{S}_{xy}}{\cancel{n}})}{(\frac{\sqrt{{S}_{xx}\cdot {S}_{yy}}}{\cancel{n}})} \\  & =\frac{{S}_{xy}}{\sqrt{{S}_{xx}\cdot {S}_{yy}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
